---
name: independent-ac-verifier
description: "Use when a managed task needs a separate acceptance judgment against the original request, current contract and actual profile-specific evidence."
---

# Independent acceptance

Apply relevant [evidence decisions](../task-orchestrator/references/evidence-decisions.md): actual target/reference authority, required dependency postconditions and current artifact purpose/version. For migration/optimization assess meaningful equivalence and relevant boundaries/preexisting ambiguity. Metadata or prepared drafts are not consumer/execution evidence. Missing relevant code is a coverage gap to investigate or disclose; it does not establish absent behavior.

Act in a separate session from implementation. Read the original request and sources, approved proposal/stages, acceptance obligations, current artifacts and actual executed evidence. Inspect the delivered result directly; an implementation summary is only a locator.

For each criterion report its ID, expected behavior, source/evidence references, verification method, PASS/FAIL/UNVERIFIED/BLOCKED/NOT_APPLICABLE, limitations and missing coverage. Mandatory unexecuted checks cannot PASS. Do not weaken acceptance to fit the implementation or infer a real resource/document/model run from a fixture.

For configured software test adequacy, inspect the separate scenario/consumer-boundary assessment and its missing coverage. Independently identify materially omitted risks; positive counts or an adequate verdict alone do not establish original behavior. An ordinary AC receipt cannot substitute for the distinct adequacy execution.

Use missing_coverage only for unmet proof required by this configured criterion at this gate. Any nonempty value blocks a mandatory criterion even if status says PASS. Put nonblocking coverage limits and mandatory later delivery inputs/effects in limitations and the pending delivery plan; they do not become prerequisites for current source approval. A real current evidence gap remains UNVERIFIED/BLOCKED. Passing a source criterion never establishes later publication or overall completion.

Apply task-orchestrator's [profile evidence](../task-orchestrator/references/profile-evidence.md). Software retains mandatory successful commands, positive actual test counts, no skipped required tests and current source/contract/plan fingerprints. Documents, research and infrastructure need substantive independent evaluation of their own deliverables. Suggest AC-derived checks independently of implementation assumptions.

Use `ase --project PROJECT verify TASK` through the authorized local backend adapter to capture independent receipts. A missing optional integration is not a prerequisite; unavailable independent-session capability is an explicit blocker. Do not manufacture receipts, copy credentials or relax permissions. Separate model judgment does not establish a separate OS security identity.

# Evidence, readiness and decisions

Use relevant sections for comparisons, blockers, dependencies, actionable artifacts, semantic changes or review findings. This refines the existing workflow; it adds no universal form, new approval or mandatory service. Clear authorized work proceeds. Use the [evidence brief](../assets/evidence-brief.md) when several material facts must stay aligned; otherwise retain them in existing notes.

## 1. Establish the target and reference

Identify the actual resource and relevant environment, tenant/account and consumer. For a comparison or migration, identify the reference's role and why it is authoritative for the requested result: an applicable owner decision, contract or verified provenance. Record its locator and current version. Deployed configuration proves what is used; availability, similar names and a colleague's implementation do not prove the right business baseline.

Separate inherited behavior/settings from changes introduced by this task. Reuse compatible project conventions; avoid an override solely because an inherited value differs from a guess. Investigate a material conflict with the approved target. Escalate an unresolved owner-only choice using the existing short question format. An unconfirmed reference does not authorize changing the target or unrelated systems.

## 2. Bound the claim and prove the blocker

A blocking claim names the required outcome, affected stage/dependents, and actual observation: operation, target, safe account/access-method reference, time/version, result and inspected scope. Keep credentials and raw responses out of notes. Distinguish a known failure from an unperformed check.

"Object not found in schema S with account A" is bounded evidence. "The object does not exist" needs corresponding coverage. One denied login or failed optional adapter does not prove the application is broken or all access is impossible. Try a concrete useful authorized alternative when available; an optional integration failure does not block usable CLI/file work. Do not request new access or change permissions silently.

Continue research while a specific lead can distinguish hypotheses. Stop on sufficient evidence, no useful lead, unavailable required access, an owner-only decision or an explicit stop/limit. Record the stopping reason and remaining unknowns; exhausted inspected sources are not absence everywhere. Then proceed with a supported in-scope choice or ask one material question: checked facts, unconfirmed hypothesis, recommendation/reason and decision needed. Hold affected work and continue independent approved work. Reconcile UNKNOWN external effects rather than replaying them.

## 3. Check the readiness the obligation actually needs

These are separate observations, not an automatic promotion ladder:

| Observation | What it establishes |
| --- | --- |
| Promised/announced | Delivery is unverified. |
| Exists/visible in metadata | The object/configuration is visible in the inspected scope. |
| Usable by intended account | The required authorized operation actually succeeds through the relevant access path. |
| Structurally complete | Required fields, interfaces and version are present. |
| Data suitable for this task | Bounded actual data/postconditions meet the task requirements. |
| Consumer behavior verified | A meaningful consumer-level check demonstrates required behavior. |

Record only the levels needed for the affected obligation, with evidence and unknowns. Installed tools are not usable sessions. Metadata is not a successful SELECT. Readable empty data is valid when the contract allows emptiness; it is not proof of representative data or correct calculations. Probe the relevant intended account/consumer within existing authority; do not broaden access or copy secrets. Once required postconditions are evidenced, proceed without a ceremonial checklist or new approval.

Bind required proof to the phase and action that can produce it. A current gate judges evidence causally attainable before its authorization; a criterion it judges must not require that same AC/review/gate approval or the later effects that approval authorizes. Independent AC/review and the current APPROVED gate remain mandatory authorization checks. If proof depends on the authorized action, retain that obligation as mandatory later work, leave its result pending, and verify it after the action before declaring the overall assignment complete.

If Publisher requires the whole-task gate, moving later proof to another stage of that same task does not remove the cycle. Scope its gated contract to source acceptance and retain the later mandatory obligations in an explicit publication/finish plan or separate delivery task. As applicable, these include actual publication, intended-consumer postconditions, matching remote/local SHA and dated closure. Source approval alone does not complete the overall assignment. Correcting this phase allocation within existing authorized scope needs no new approval; preserve every original obligation, independent verification and the gate, and never label future evidence PASS.

## 4. Separate artifact purpose, state and version

For an artifact that may be executed, handed off or used as evidence, retain:

- Purpose: discussion draft, reference/example, or intended execution/delivery.
- State: draft, prepared, applied/delivered, or independently verified, supported by actual evidence.
- Identity: path/object, content hash or meaningful version, target and relevant requirement/dependency source versions.
- Unresolved placeholders/assumptions and the current next action.

A reference CREATE script for an existing object is not a command to execute. Prepared text is not an applied resource. A filename such as final.sql is not readiness evidence. Before authorized execution or execution-ready handoff, inspect exact current bytes/version, target, required inputs and unresolved placeholders. A legitimate runtime parameter is not an unresolved placeholder. Check copied text for meaningful encoding/invisible-character corruption; do not strip whitespace or rewrite strings/identifiers blindly. Reuse authorization when its scope still applies; preparation/verification grants no external action by itself.

After a material answer or changed source, identify affected assumptions, artifact versions, acceptance checks and cached conclusions. Refresh these and their dependents, mark old versions historical/superseded, and update the current brief before the next action. Keep unaffected work valid and preserve evidence of already-applied effects; refreshing a draft does not authorize replay. Use existing intake/checkpoint/knowledge fields and source references. The brief is an optional view, not a new schema or second tracker.

## 5. Verify meaning when changing implementation

For migration, translation or optimization, identify required preserved behavior and its authority. Compare old/reference and proposed behavior using relevant examples: normal/boundary cases, null/missing values, duplicates, errors, ordering, rounding/units/time windows or permission effects as applicable. Use meaningful differential checks and the actual consumer contract. HTTP success, matching columns or one happy-path row alone do not prove equivalence.

A documented platform capability is a hypothesis about this execution path until checked. A narrowing filter needs evidence that excluded data cannot affect the required result. Separate a new regression from ambiguity already in the reference. Preserve supported behavior within scope; do not silently invent a business rule to resolve ambiguity. Hold only a material unresolved choice and its dependents, with a concise recommendation; continue independent work.

## 6. Substantiate and respond to review

Before asserting an actionable defect, trace a concrete trigger through the relevant caller, callee and contract; cite the inspected location or observation supporting the consequence. Tests and actual error paths can establish whether a guard/transition exists. An omitted callee means missing coverage, not proof of absent behavior: obtain relevant code if authorized, or report a material gap as UNVERIFIED/BLOCKED without inventing a defect.

Before repair, verify the finding against current code/evidence. Reproduce or otherwise establish the actual consequence. Repair confirmed in-scope defects, then rerun affected checks and fresh independent AC/review. Reject a disproven finding with evidence and retain the finding/response in history. Avoid speculative changes or downgrading a real P0/P1/P2 to obtain approval. Existing scope, recovery and separate-session requirements remain in force.

# Profile evidence

Select a profile by the requested action. A finance report's data warnings are not software debugging; changing the generating code is software. Mixed tasks map every obligation to stages and child tasks without weakening parent coverage.

Apply the [readiness proof boundary](evidence-decisions.md#3-check-the-readiness-the-obligation-actually-needs) when allocating profile evidence. Current acceptance uses proof causally attainable before its gate; later authorized effects remain mandatory in the publication/finish plan or delivery task and pending until checked. A whole-task publication gate includes all its stages, so stage reassignment alone cannot separate future proof. Phase-local source approval does not establish publication, postconditions or overall completion.

| Profile | Evidence to collect |
| --- | --- |
| software | Executed mandatory commands, positive test counts, no skipped required tests, independent AC and code review, current source/contract/plan fingerprints |
| infrastructure | Actual resource identity, before/after observations, operation intent and reconciliation, independent postcondition evidence; no invented resource success |
| document | Required artifact, readable rendering/structure where applicable, required content and traceable sources, independent acceptance and substantive review |
| research | Sources and dates, claim-to-source coverage, clear inference and uncertainty, independent acceptance and substantive review |
| mixed | Required parent coverage across all child profiles and stages; no completed parent while mandatory children remain unresolved |

Configured evaluators determine executed facts; model judgments remain separate. Manual confirmation counts only when explicitly specified as a criterion, with its source. A protocol test establishes the protocol only. Missing mandatory resources or independent execution remain BLOCKED. Local reliability records do not enforce publishing against another process with the same OS identity; trusted CI and server rules are required for that boundary.

Check source versions and current observations: Git commit alone does not cover dirty/untracked bytes, external settings or non-Git workspaces. Refresh affected records and their transitive dependents; retain historical provenance and explicit unknowns. Unknown is unavailable until probed. For Codex, Claude and Copilot use their local adapters where authorized. Protocol fixtures and native role files do not prove live execution. Check native subagent availability, permission and current capacity separately from formal Runner verification. When independent ready work can benefit, read task-orchestrator's [parallel work](../task-orchestrator/references/parallel-work.md), map prerequisites and ownership, and refresh the ready set as results arrive. Missing optional native delegation selects serial work; it does not by itself block the task.

Re-evaluate understanding and gaps after discovery and each material answer. Report inspected evidence, reuse, remaining uncertainty and actual limitations; refresh only affected assumptions and dependent evidence. Map explicit gaps to affected known stages and their dependents; ambiguous mappings stay conservative. Independent approved work can continue. ---
name: task-orchestrator
description: "Use when a managed software, infrastructure, document, research or mixed task is requested in an explicitly adopted project or workspace."
---

# Managed task workflow

For comparisons, blockers, dependencies, actionable artifacts, semantic changes or disputed review findings, apply relevant [evidence decisions](references/evidence-decisions.md). Confirm target/reference authority, required readiness and current artifact purpose/version. Preserve required semantics and substantiate findings through actual callees/evidence before repair. Clear tasks need no new questionnaire or approval.

Use only in a project or workspace that explicitly adopted DevelopmentFramework. Adoption covers managed software, infrastructure, documents, research and mixed work; select the profile from the actual action. A financial report with warnings is a document or research task. A requested fix to its generator is software. Ordinary questions use their domain workflow without creating a managed task.

Read task-intake for new assignments and task-discovery before proposing implementation. Its scoped search for existing project examples is the default; an explicit user opt-out skips that search and example reuse, including cached/delegated examples. Preserve that choice before retrieving pattern records; necessary target/dependency inspection remains. Restore an existing task with `ase --project PROJECT restore TASK` before replacing it. Local SQLite records, sources and checkpoints are shared across backends on this computer and isolated by project identity.

Before any clarification, distinguish a retrievable fact about the existing target from a decision only the owner can make. Inspect supplied context and fresh relevant memory, then use task-discovery's [answer investigation](../task-discovery/references/answer-investigation.md) and available authorized read-only checks for factual gaps. A detail missing from the prompt is not itself an access or requirements blocker. Ask only after the relevant evidence/next useful checks cannot resolve the material gap, or the owner alone must choose; give actual checked facts and a concise supported hypothesis/recommendation.

A clear assignment authorizes immediate execution within its scope. After checking obvious gaps and fresh relevant context, record a concise internal proposal and the original assignment's authorization against its exact version/stages; proceed without another approval interview. Re-evaluate gaps after discovery and material answers, refresh affected assumptions/evidence, and keep independently approved stages moving. Read [questions and approval](references/questions-and-approval.md) for unresolved business/access/authority decisions or serious architectural changes beyond scope; routine technical choices stay autonomous.

Execute through the local `ase` CLI using the configured backend adapter and appropriate domain skills. When `.devframework/config.toml` selects project-local mode, use that project's `.devframework/bin/ase.ps1` or `.devframework/bin/ase`; its three bots share private state inside that project. Do not replace it with another project's/global home on an unknown UUID. The CLI is sufficient; a missing optional integration is not a workflow blocker. Discover actual independent-session capability and permission before promising verification. An installed skill or a protocol fixture does not establish live backend availability. Do not copy credentials or change provider permissions to make a missing capability appear available.

When an approved external service needs authentication, read [local credentials](references/local-credentials.md). Use shared metadata and credential references; import only a user-designated local file, let the local executor handle values, and reuse sessions/approval. Configure a supported CLI recipe within the approved bounds before asking the user to solve a technical setup detail. Credentials do not expand task authority.

When two or more ready parts are independent and useful to run together, use available permitted native subagents under [parallel work](references/parallel-work.md). Record the actual native handle and sealed result; coordinator acceptance remains separate from independent AC/review. Recompute ready work after results and dependencies; preserve original authority, root ownership and budgets. Unknown launches require reconciliation, never a replacement based on timeout. Serial fallback remains available when optional delegation is unavailable.

Keep the original chat as lead and process its durable [coordinator inbox](references/coordinator-events.md) after results and before completion. Return evidence to that exact coordinator through available native tools or its local inbox. Commit dispatch/processing intents before effects; recover and reconcile original attempts. Notifications never expand user authority or launch another lead. Successful informational events do not trigger endless verification loops.

For software, enable explicit test adequacy and save a requirement/risk scenario plan before implementation under [test adequacy](../quality-gate/references/test-adequacy.md). After meaningful executed checks, obtain a separate independent adequacy assessment alongside AC/review; positive counts alone are insufficient. Investigate/repair current coverage gaps without waiting for an extra owner prompt. Excluding tests from publication still allows required local testing.

Run meaningful checks and separate independent acceptance and substantive review against the original request. For software preserve positive executed test counts, successful mandatory checks and independent AC/code review. P0/P1/P2 block approval; P3 is advisory. Use `ase --project PROJECT gate TASK` and `report TASK`; a process finishing or a written PASS is not approval. Read [profile evidence](references/profile-evidence.md) when selecting checks.

Repair actionable in-scope findings, then rerun affected checks and fresh independent AC/review against current artifacts; avoid unrelated refactoring. New progress-mode tasks reassess after three consecutive unsuccessful cycles without verified progress on the same underlying problem, rather than stopping after three total cycles. Verified progress means newly satisfied original obligations or verified failure elimination; prose, edits and renamed stages do not count. Resume/delegates share history. A supported diagnostic probe may continue; failure without verified progress stops automatic mutation. Preserve explicit hard limits and saved legacy policies. Unresolved blockers hold affected work. Reconcile UNKNOWN external effects before retrying; nonvisibility alone is insufficient. Read [stopping and recovery](references/stopping-and-recovery.md) for the full rules.

At completion, awaiting approval, blocker, pause, cancellation or requested stop, save a dated session closure and one exact next action. Read [finish and reports](references/finish-and-reports.md). Close a session without claiming the task completed. Publish or send only under the existing explicit destination authorization; default publication remains a dry run.

As applicable, these include actual publication, intended-consumer postconditions, matching remote/local SHA and dated closure. Source approval alone does not complete the overall assignment. Correcting this phase allocation within existing authorized scope needs no new approval; preserve every original obligation, independent verification and the gate, and never label future evidence PASS.

## 4. Separate artifact purpose, state and version

For an artifact that may be executed, handed off or used as evidence, retain:

- Purpose: discussion draft, reference/example, or intended execution/delivery.
- State: draft, prepared, applied/delivered, or independently verified, supported by actual evidence.
- Identity: path/object, content hash or meaningful version, target and relevant requirement/dependency source versions.
- Unresolved placeholders/assumptions and the current next action.

A reference CREATE script for an existing object is not a command to execute. Prepared text is not an applied resource. A filename such as final.sql is not readiness evidence. Before authorized execution or execution-ready handoff, inspect exact current bytes/version, target, required inputs and unresolved placeholders. A legitimate runtime parameter is not an unresolved placeholder. Check copied text for meaningful encoding/invisible-character corruption; do not strip whitespace or rewrite strings/identifiers blindly. Reuse authorization when its scope still applies; preparation/verification grants no external action by itself.

After a material answer or changed source, identify affected assumptions, artifact versions, acceptance checks and cached conclusions. Refresh these and their dependents, mark old versions historical/superseded, and update the current brief before the next action. Keep unaffected work valid and preserve evidence of already-applied effects; refreshing a draft does not authorize replay. Use existing intake/checkpoint/knowledge fields and source references. The brief is an optional view, not a new schema or second tracker.

## 5. Verify meaning when changing implementation

For migration, translation or optimization, identify required preserved behavior and its authority. Compare old/reference and proposed behavior using relevant examples: normal/boundary cases, null/missing values, duplicates, errors, ordering, rounding/units/time windows or permission effects as applicable. Use meaningful differential checks and the actual consumer contract. HTTP success, matching columns or one happy-path row alone do not prove equivalence.

A documented platform capability is a hypothesis about this execution path until checked. A narrowing filter needs evidence that excluded data cannot affect the required result. Separate a new regression from ambiguity already in the reference. Preserve supported behavior within scope; do not silently invent a business rule to resolve ambiguity. Hold only a material unresolved choice and its dependents, with a concise recommendation; continue independent work.

## 6. Substantiate and respond to review

Before asserting an actionable defect, trace a concrete trigger through the relevant caller, callee and contract; cite the inspected location or observation supporting the consequence. Tests and actual error paths can establish whether a guard/transition exists. An omitted callee means missing coverage, not proof of absent behavior: obtain relevant code if authorized, or report a material gap as UNVERIFIED/BLOCKED without inventing a defect.

Before repair, verify the finding against current code/evidence. Reproduce or otherwise establish the actual consequence. Repair confirmed in-scope defects, then rerun affected checks and fresh independent AC/review. Reject a disproven finding with evidence and retain the finding/response in history. Avoid speculative changes or downgrading a real P0/P1/P2 to obtain approval. Existing scope, recovery and separate-session requirements remain in force.

For other profiles use task-orchestrator's [profile evidence](../task-orchestrator/references/profile-evidence.md) and review the artifact, claims or actual resource postconditions; code-only checks do not replace that review.

Use authorized local `ase` independent-session adapters for genuine runner receipts. Fixtures and descriptors prove only their protocol/structure. Blocking findings require in-scope repair, fresh checks and new independent AC/review against changed source. Preserve persisted root/stage budgets and authorization; unresolved infrastructure or scope blockers stop automatic mutation.

# Evidence, readiness and decisions

Use relevant sections for comparisons, blockers, dependencies, actionable artifacts, semantic changes or review findings. Investigate a material conflict with the approved target. Escalate an unresolved owner-only choice using the existing short question format. An unconfirmed reference does not authorize changing the target or unrelated systems.

## 2. Bound the claim and prove the blocker

"Object not found in schema S with account A" is bounded evidence. "The object does not exist" needs corresponding coverage. One denied login or failed optional adapter does not prove the application is broken or all access is impossible. Try a concrete useful authorized alternative when available; an optional integration failure does not block usable CLI/file work. Do not request new access or change permissions silently.

Continue research while a specific lead can distinguish hypotheses. Stop on sufficient evidence, no useful lead, unavailable required access, an owner-only decision or an explicit stop/limit. Record the stopping reason and remaining unknowns; exhausted inspected sources are not absence everywhere. Then proceed with a supported in-scope choice or ask one material question: checked facts, unconfirmed hypothesis, recommendation/reason and decision needed. Hold affected work and continue independent approved work. Reconcile UNKNOWN external effects rather than replaying them.

| Observation | What it establishes |
| --- | --- |
| Promised/announced | Delivery is unverified. |
| Exists/visible in metadata | The object/configuration is visible in the inspected scope. |
| Usable by intended account | The required authorized operation actually succeeds through the relevant access path. |
| Structurally complete | Required fields, interfaces and version are present. |
| Data suitable for this task | Bounded actual data/postconditions meet the task requirements. |
| Consumer behavior verified | A meaningful consumer-level check demonstrates required behavior. |

Readable empty data is valid when the contract allows emptiness; it is not proof of representative data or correct calculations. Probe the relevant intended account/consumer within existing authority; do not broaden access or copy secrets. Once required postconditions are evidenced, proceed without a ceremonial checklist or new approval.

Bind required proof to the phase and action that can produce it. A current gate judges evidence causally attainable before its authorization; a criterion it judges must not require that same AC/review/gate approval or the later effects that approval authorizes. Independent AC/review and the current APPROVED gate remain mandatory authorization checks. If proof depends on the authorized action, retain that obligation as mandatory later work, leave its result pending, and verify it after the action before declaring the overall assignment complete.

# Profile evidence

Select a profile by the requested action. A finance report's data warnings are not software debugging; changing the generating code is software. Mixed tasks map every obligation to stages and child tasks without weakening parent coverage.

Apply the [readiness proof boundary](evidence-decisions.md#3-check-the-readiness-the-obligation-actually-needs) when allocating profile evidence. Current acceptance uses proof causally attainable before its gate; later authorized effects remain mandatory in the publication/finish plan or delivery task and pending until checked. A whole-task publication gate includes all its stages, so stage reassignment alone cannot separate future proof. Phase-local source approval does not establish publication, postconditions or overall completion.

| Profile | Evidence to collect |
| --- | --- |
| software | Executed mandatory commands, positive test counts, no skipped required tests, independent AC and code review, current source/contract/plan fingerprints |
| infrastructure | Actual resource identity, before/after observations, operation intent and reconciliation, independent postcondition evidence; no invented resource success |
| document | Required artifact, readable rendering/structure where applicable, required content and traceable sources, independent acceptance and substantive review |
| research | Sources and dates, claim-to-source coverage, clear inference and uncertainty, independent acceptance and substantive review |
| mixed | Required parent coverage across all child profiles and stages; no completed parent while mandatory children remain unresolved |

Configured evaluators determine executed facts; model judgments remain separate. Manual confirmation counts only when explicitly specified as a criterion, with its source. A protocol test establishes the protocol only. Missing mandatory resources or independent execution remain BLOCKED. Local reliability records do not enforce publishing against another process with the same OS identity; trusted CI and server rules are required for that boundary.

# Test adequacy before software completion

Use for software and software stages of mixed tasks. A large passing test count establishes executed examples; judge whether those examples can catch plausible violations of the original requirements.

New software tasks created through the CLI enable `test_adequacy: {"version":1,"required":true}`. Programmatic task creators must carry that explicit policy. Preserve saved contracts and label old unconfigured adequacy honestly. A request to exclude tests from a commit/PR concerns publication; it does not remove local testing or adequacy obligations.

## Before implementation

Inspect current code, relevant existing tests, project examples and actual available test tools. Derive a concise scenario plan from original acceptance and relevant failure risks. Every mandatory software criterion/stage needs a required scenario. Save it through `ase adequacy plan TASK --file plan.json --expected-revision N`.

Each scenario has `id`, `acceptance_ids`, `risk`, `boundary`, `expected`, `evidence_ids`, `required`. The plan also contains `not_applicable` rows with `risk` and a source-supported `reason`. Choose meaningful scenarios rather than an exhaustive checklist. Keep ordinary technical choices autonomous.

Examples of relevant boundaries:

| Requirement/risk | Discriminating evidence |
| --- | --- |
| Two workers must not process the same item | Real concurrent workers/connections synchronized at the competing operation; one claim/effect, including restart. Sequential calls through one stub do not exercise the race. |
| State/permissions can change during I/O | Pause at the relevant boundary, change the state, resume and observe the required externally visible result. Initially-private fixtures alone do not cover Public to Private during a read. |
| Select latest version | Equal ordering keys, duplicates, missing values and insertion orders when relevant. Distinct timestamps alone do not cover ties. |
| HTTP validation/status | Request through the actual HTTP boundary and inspect response/status/persistence. A handler exception alone does not establish what a caller receives. |
| SQL claim/transaction semantics | Actual supported database/connection behavior for the relevant transaction; an in-memory mock alone cannot establish database concurrency. |
| Retry/crash/external effect | Lost acknowledgement, known/unknown application, deduplication and recovery of the same operation. A missing observation is not nonapplication. |

Record only applicable risks. A local file operation does not need an invented HTTP test. If the approved environment cannot supply a required boundary, identify exactly which result remains unverified and seek a useful authorized alternative before asking the owner.

## Independent assessment

After actual checks, run the configured independent adequacy session in addition to ordinary AC and substantive review. It uses a separate captured execution/provider session and examines original requirements, plan, actual test source/assertions, executed logs, relevant production paths and current evidence. Implementation summaries and test names alone are locators.

When `handoff.purpose` is `test_adequacy`, return the configured adequacy schema. Evaluate each planned scenario and add relevant omitted scenarios independently. For every PASS supply current check IDs, test source, test IDs and the assertion that discriminates the failure. Report missing required boundary/source evidence as UNVERIFIED/BLOCKED; confirmed violated behavior is FAIL. A boolean adequate, a large count, source text containing a test name or a mocked success cannot substitute for actual proof. Do not claim exhaustive bug absence.

The runtime binds the assessment to the exact plan, source, contract, proposal, checks and relevant stage/context. Missing, insufficient, reused or stale assessment blocks configured completion. A passing source assessment does not establish publication or future deployment results.

The original lead handles current coverage gaps/findings without waiting for the owner to say "check edge cases". Confirm findings, repair in scope, execute affected tests and obtain fresh independent judgments. Preserve the existing progress-sensitive stop/reassessment rules; do not loop until another model says PASS. Ask only for material remaining owner decisions, unavailable required access or scope changes, with a short checked-evidence hypothesis and recommendation.
